description: Migrate the Python scraper storage layer to SQLAlchemy 2.0 that MAPS to the Drizzle-created tables from FEAT-001 (no DDL, no Alembic, no create_all). Replace the three json_store call sites (engine.py, simulator.py, routers/scraper.py) with SQLAlchemy queries against the shared DB via DATABASE_URL, handle the unused audit mirror (jsonl_append.py), and update scraper deps/tests. DEPENDS ON FEAT-001: the tables and column names defined there are the contract this FEAT conforms to.
steps: Add dependencies to scraper/requirements.txt: SQLAlchemy>=2.0 and a Postgres driver (psycopg[binary] or psycopg2-binary). Add DATABASE_URL handling to scraper/app/config.py (Settings.database_url from env) and to scraper/.env.example.

Create scraper/app/storage/db.py: a SQLAlchemy 2.0 engine/session factory built from settings.database_url, and SQLAlchemy models (declarative) that MAP to the EXISTING Drizzle tables from FEAT-001 — use the SAME table and column names (snake_case per the FEAT-001 schema). Models: Insurer, Plan, Source, Thread, ThreadMessage, ScraperRun (and AuditEntry if needed). Do NOT call create_all / do not emit DDL — mapping only. Confirm column names against web/src/lib/schema.ts produced by FEAT-001 (read context.json + FEAT-001 findings).

Refactor scraper/app/scraper/engine.py: replace read_json(sources)/read_json(plans)/write_json/append_jsonl(runs) with SQLAlchemy queries — load sources and plans from DB, update/insert plans and sources within a transaction (only persist when changed>0, preserving the 'failed scrape never deletes last good data' invariant), and insert the ScraperRun row. Preserve the existing dict field access the pipeline relies on (map DB rows to the shapes change_detector/converter/validator expect, or refactor them to use model attributes). Keep _save_versioned writing HTML to data/versions on the filesystem (unchanged).

Refactor scraper/app/personas/simulator.py: replace read_json(threads)/read_json(insurers)/write_json(threads) with SQLAlchemy — load the thread + insurer, append the inbound ThreadMessage row, update thread status/riskFlags/updatedAt in a transaction. Preserve persona dispatch and the slow-persona no-reply path.
Refactor scraper/app/routers/scraper.py: replace read_jsonl(scraper_runs.jsonl) with a SQLAlchemy query for the latest ScraperRun (ORDER BY started_at or an id DESC) for the /scraper/status endpoint.

Handle scraper/app/storage/jsonl_append.py (the unused audit hash-chain mirror, no callers): either delete it, or if kept, update it to match the FEAT-001 audit contract (exact key order timestamp,actor,action,detail,prevHash; compact serialization) and document that the web app is the sole audit writer. Recommend deletion to avoid a divergent second writer; note the choice in findings.

Decide the fate of scraper/app/storage/json_store.py: remove it if no longer referenced after the refactor, or keep only if something still needs file IO (versions/ is written directly via Path in engine.py, so json_store likely becomes dead — remove and update imports).

Update scraper tests (pytest, ./dev.sh test) and the scraper Dockerfile/requirements as needed so the suite runs against the DB. Any test that previously wrote JSON files must seed/clean the test database instead. Keep the hash-chain / change-detection / PII tests passing.
Append a TASK.MD entry summarizing the scraper SQLAlchemy mapping, noting it conforms to the FEAT-001 Drizzle schema and that SQLAlchemy performs no DDL.
acceptance_criteria: scraper/requirements.txt includes SQLAlchemy>=2.0 and a Postgres driver; scraper/app/config.py exposes database_url from env; scraper/.env.example documents DATABASE_URL.
SQLAlchemy models map to the FEAT-001 tables with matching table/column names and perform NO DDL (no create_all, no Alembic).

engine.py, simulator.py, routers/scraper.py no longer import from app.storage.json_store; the scrape pipeline reads/writes plans/sources/scraper_runs via SQLAlchemy and still preserves 'a failed scrape never deletes last good data'.
`./dev.sh lint` passes (ruff) and `./dev.sh test` passes against a disposable Postgres seeded with FEAT-001's seed data.
jsonl_append.py is deleted (or reconciled to the FEAT-001 audit contract) and json_store.py removed if unreferenced; no dangling imports remain.
Running the scraper (run_now / simulate_reply) end-to-end against the shared DB updates plans/threads/scraper_runs rows and the web app reads the same data.
verification: Integration: with FEAT-001 migrations applied and seed loaded on a disposable Postgres, trigger a scrape (POST /scraper/run or run_scraper) and a reply (simulate_reply), then confirm the DB rows updated and the web endpoints (/api/plans, /api/crm/threads, /api/scraper/status) reflect the changes
